column2: The Dark Gods Call

A rider in blackened mail comes to my hall with a message from [From.GetTitledName]. [From.GetSheHeCap] has claimed the right to call a Black Crusade and asks every warband of the faith to gather under [From.GetHerHis] banner.

The horde will fall upon [crusade_title.GetBaseName], held by [crusade_character.GetCrusadeReligionDescription] [crusade_character.GetTitledName]. It is time they learned what it costs to defy the gods.

The target is not yet set in iron. A strong warlord who marches with the horde could turn it toward a prize of more use to us.
I will think on it.
The Black Crusade gathers its strength.
My warriors are ready! To [crusade_title.GetBaseName]!
May the gods watch my fellow [Root.Religion.GetGroupName] in their slaughter.
Black Crusade for [crusade_title.GetBaseName]

The ground shakes under hoof and boot as the hosts of Chaos march south on the Black Crusade for [crusade_title.GetBaseName]. [Root.GetCrusadeLaunchFirstPart]

[Root.GetCrusadeLaunchSecondPart]

[From.Religion.GetHighGodName] will reward every warrior who wades into the slaughter.
For the Dark Gods!
The Black Crusade for [crusade_title.GetName] begins.
The northern hordes are upon us!
The Horde Turns Back

The call went out to every corner of the North, and it was not needed. Our target had worshipped the gods in secret all along, and with the horde at the border chose to declare it rather than burn.\n\nThe warlord must find other prey.
The gods are not amused.
The Black Crusade has been called off.
[Root.GetTitledName]\nYou have not yet taken up the banner. You owe me a debt, and I am calling it in. Gather your warriors and join the horde.\n[From.GetTitledName]
Then I will march.

[pleased_courtier.GetFirstName] stops me on my way out of the hall to tell me how glad [pleased_courtier.GetSheHe] was to hear I have pledged my warriors to the Black Crusade, and wishes me good slaughter.
Your words are welcome.
A letter from [pleased_participant.GetTitledName] praises my choice to march with the horde. Perhaps we should stand shoulder to shoulder when the killing starts.
A worthy sentiment.
Let us kill side by side!

A letter comes from the despicable [pleased_participant.GetTitledName]. Since we both march on [crusade_title.GetName], [pleased_participant.GetSheHe] proposes that we bury our feud until the war is done.
The gods favour the united. For now.
I would sooner put an axe in your back.

I cannot hide my hunger for the coming war. When I think of [crusade_title.GetName] burning I feel the gods closer than ever before. I never thought myself a zealot of the [Root.Religion.GetGroupName], but perhaps the gods are changing me.
Blood for the gods!

Before I leave for the war I spend a day by the water with the old thing that lives in it. It has many fine ideas about the coming battles for [crusade_title.GetName]. I am blessed to have such a friend.
Before I leave I walk out into the woods to sit with the beasts. I end up in a long talk with... well, I am not sure what it was, but it had a great deal of sense to share!
I will do my utmost!
An eye for your wisdom, you say?
We will meet again!

[displeased_courtier.GetFirstName] tells me at length exactly how ashamed [displeased_courtier.GetSheHe] is that I have broken my pledge to the horde. When the tirade is over [displeased_courtier.GetSheHe] finally leaves me in peace.
How dare [displeased_courtier.GetSheHe]?!
Perhaps it was the wrong choice.
A letter from [displeased_participant.GetTitledName]: [displeased_participant.GetSheHe] has heard I broke my pledge to the Black Crusade and no longer trusts my word.
That is none of [displeased_participant.GetHerHis] business.
A messenger brings a letter from [displeased_participant.GetTitledName], calling me a coward and an oath-breaker who has betrayed every [Root.Religion.GetGroupName] warrior in the horde.
Then let us be enemies!
Oath-Breaker

Riders go to every war camp in the North: [From.GetTitledName] has cast out the faithless [unpledging_actor.GetTitledName], who swore to march on [crusade_title.GetName] and then turned [unpledging_actor.GetHerHis] back on the horde.\n\nThe gods do not forgive the coward. [unpledging_actor.GetSheHeCap] is to be given no shelter and no mercy, and whoever takes [unpledging_actor.GetHerHis] head will be thought well of.
Faithless dog.
What did [From.GetSheHe] call me!?

[Root.GetTitledName]\nYou have still not pledged your warriors to the horde. Every warband of the [Root.Religion.GetGroupName] is wanted for the war on [crusade_title.GetName]. Join us, or send gold if you are too weak to fight.\n[From.GetTitledName]
My warriors will march.
I will send gold instead.
I need time to decide.
Neither marching nor paying may have dire consequences.
The New [new_crusader_king.GetKingQueen]

The long war for [new_crusader_king.PrimaryTitle.GetName] is over, and the land is the gods' at last. [new_crusader_king.GetDynName] has taken its throne as the beneficiary of [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName], [new_crusader_king.GetKingQueen] of a realm carved from the enemy's flesh. Holding it on the edge of the Old World will be bloody work, but all agree [new_crusader_king.GetTitledFirstName] has the strength for it.\n\nThe warlord commands the rest of the faithful to stand by this new realm, and not to let it fall back to the weak.
May [new_crusader_king.GetSheHe] hold it.
If only it had been me...
[Root.GetTitledName]\nI have not forgotten our quarrel, but you have come back to the horde when it matters. The curse on your name is lifted.\n[From.GetTitledName]
The gods are merciful. This once.
The [beneficiary_check_crusader_beneficiary.GetLordLady] of [beneficiary_check_crusader_beneficiary.PrimaryTitle.GetName]

The war was hard won, but the burning is over and the lands I fought for went to [beneficiary_check_crusader_beneficiary.GetDynName]. Holding a fief in the conquered realm will be no easy life, and I wish [beneficiary_check_crusader_beneficiary.GetHerHim] good fortune.\n\nAs my warband rides out of [beneficiary_check_crusader_beneficiary.PrimaryTitle.GetName] I look back once. I wonder what my life would have been had I stayed in [beneficiary_check_crusader_beneficiary.GetDynName]'s place.
No. [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName] is my home.
Perhaps in another life.

Greetings, [Root.GetTitledName]

I have heard that the servants of the Dark Gods have called a Black Crusade against your lands. As a fellow [From.Religion.GetName], I will stand at your side when the hordes come.
[From.GetTitledName]
I thank you, [From.GetTitledFirstName].
How much gold should I give to the Black Crusade's war chest?
A small offering. The gods will remember it.
I know just how much.
A gift worthy of my name!
I cannot spare anything.
If the Black Crusade is won, who should rule the conquered lands? I could leave it to the warlord, give the land to my beneficiary, or keep it for myself.
The warlord will decide.
If the Black Crusade is won, the warlord grants the lands to the §YChosen Lord§!. If there is none, they go to the §YBeneficiary§! of the lord who did most in the war.
My beneficiary will take them.
If the Black Crusade is won and I did most in the war, the lands go to my §YBeneficiary§!.
Why would I give MY conquest away?
If the Black Crusade is won and I did most in the war, I take the lands myself.
I will keep to my choice.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! is dead. I must find another.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! has gained land and can no longer be my beneficiary.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! is now heir to a landed title and can no longer be my beneficiary.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! has become a mercenary and can no longer be my beneficiary.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! has joined a holy order and can no longer be my beneficiary.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! is too young to be my beneficiary.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! is too sick to be my beneficiary.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! has become a [old_crusade_beneficiary.GetAscetic] and can no longer be my beneficiary.

[Root.GetTitledName]\nKnow that I no longer favour [old_crusade_recipient.GetDynName] for the lands of [current_crusade_target_title.GetName]. When they fall they will go to [new_crusade_recipient.GetDynName].\n[From.GetTitledName]

[Root.GetTitledName]\n[old_crusade_recipient.GetDynName] is dead and will never rule [current_crusade_target_title.GetName]. When the lands fall they will go to [new_crusade_recipient.GetDynName].\n[From.GetTitledName]

[Root.GetTitledName]\n[old_crusade_recipient.GetDynName] is dead and will never rule [current_crusade_target_title.GetName]. The throne will go to [old_crusade_recipient.GetHerHis] heir [new_crusade_recipient.GetDynName] instead.\n[From.GetTitledName]
[Root.GetTitledName]\n[old_crusade_recipient.GetDynName] is dead. When [current_crusade_target_title.GetName] falls, its lands will be yours.\n[From.GetTitledName]
[Root.GetTitledName]\nI have chosen you. When [current_crusade_target_title.GetName] falls, its lands will be yours.\n[From.GetTitledName]
So be it.
The gods smile on me.

[Root.GetTitledName]\nI no longer favour [old_crusade_recipient.GetDynName] for the lands of [current_crusade_target_title.GetName]. I name nobody in [old_crusade_recipient.GetHerHis] place: let the strongest of you take them.\n[From.GetTitledName]

[Root.GetTitledName]\n[old_crusade_recipient.GetDynName] is dead and will never rule [current_crusade_target_title.GetName]. I name nobody in [old_crusade_recipient.GetHerHis] place: let the strongest of you take the lands.\n[From.GetTitledName]
I know who should have them.
Every pledged lord who left the choice to the warlord will now give the lands to their own §YBeneficiary§! instead.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName]\nThe horde marches and you are not in it. The gods see the weak, and so do I.\n[From.GetTitledFirstName]
I rule my own lands, not you.

[Root.GetTitledFirstName]\nYou swore to march with the horde, and neither you nor your warriors have shed a drop of enemy blood. Lie to me again and the gods will hear of it. I expect your warband in the field.\n[From.GetTitledName]
I suppose I should go...
[Root.GetTitledFirstName]\nYou had your warning and ignored it. A lord who swears to the gods and does not fight is no servant of theirs. From this day you are cast out.\n[From.GetTitledName]
[From.GetSheHeCap] does not sound pleased...
The Black Crusade Triumphs

[From.Religion.GetHighGodName] has given [new_crusade_most_participating_member.GetTitledName] victory in the Black Crusade for [new_crusade_title.GetBaseName]. [new_crusade_target_char.GetTitledName] was beaten at every turn and has had to give up [new_crusade_target_char.GetHerHis] lands in [new_crusade_title.GetBaseName].

[Root.GetCrusadeSelfishOrNot]

With [new_crusade_target_char.GetTitledName] driven from [new_crusade_target_char.GetHerHis] old lands, more war is certain to follow.
Praise [From.Religion.GetHighGodName]!
Gods preserve us.
Once it was a land of the gods, and warlords from all across the North have gathered to take it back.
Once it was a land of the gods, and warlords from all across the North gather to fight for it once more.
It has long lain on the edge of our lands, and [From.GetTitledName] has decided it is time to show the people of [crusade_title.GetName] the true might of Chaos.
It has long lain on the edge of our lands, and [From.GetTitledName] has decided it is time to show the people of [crusade_title.GetName] the true might of Chaos once again.
It has never been a Chaos realm, but [From.GetTitledName] has decided it is time to show the people of [crusade_title.GetName] the true might of Chaos.
It has never been a Chaos realm, but [From.GetTitledName] has decided it is time to show the people of [crusade_title.GetName] the true might of Chaos once again.
Decide what happens if the Black Crusade is won and we did most to win it. Should we leave the lands to the warlord's chosen lord, give them to our beneficiary, or take them ourselves?

I will leave the conquered lands to the warlord's chosen lord.
§Y * The gods see this as the proper way.
 * The warlord will approve.
 * I receive a larger share of the war chest.§!

I will give the conquered lands to my beneficiary.
§Y * The gods neither approve nor disapprove.
 * The warlord will neither approve nor disapprove.
 * Needs a beneficiary, or it counts as taking the lands for myself.§!

I will take the conquered lands myself if I did most to win them.
§Y * A greedy choice.
 * The warlord will disapprove.
 * I receive no share of the war chest.§!
You cannot break the pledge: the warlord called in your debt.

My warriors storm the walls of [From.GetBaseName] and the last stronghold of [duchy_region.GetBaseName] falls. The land is ours from border to border.\n\nIf I settle a warband here, it will feed the horde and anchor the Black Crusade in enemy country. The other warlords will not love me if I keep it for myself, but the gods favour the strong, and the strong take what they hold.
[duchy_region.GetBaseName] belongs to [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName] now.
§Y[Root.GetTitledName]§! seizes every title in the §YDuchy of [duchy_region.GetBaseName]§!.
§YEvery lord sworn to the Black Crusade§! changes opinion of §Y[Root.GetTitledName]§! by §R-20§! for §Y10§! years (§YSelf-serving Warlord§!).
A worthy champion will hold this land for me.
§Y[current_crusade_beneficiary.GetTitledName]§! becomes the independent §Y[current_crusade_beneficiary.GetDukeDuchessCap] of [duchy_region.GetBaseName]§!, paying tribute to [Root.GetTitledName].
I leave [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName] to my heir. I will rule [duchy_region.GetBaseName] myself.
Let it burn. I want none of it.
The Dominion of [duchy_region.GetBaseName]

The horde has taken [duchy_region.GetBaseName] and settled its warbands across the land. The Black Crusade for [crusade_title.GetName] still rages, but [duchy_region.GetBaseName] is held fast by [From.GetTitledName].\n\nThe warriors of the gods take heart from [From.GetDynName], who gave up all [From.GetHerHis] old titles to rule this conquered land in person and carry the war deeper into enemy country. The realms of the [crusade_target_ruler.Religion.GetGroupName] faithful will fall one by one.
Blood for the gods!
Let us see how long the dominion stands...
Cursed servants of Chaos!
I will miss [From.GetFirstName]...
The Dominion of [duchy_region.GetBaseName]

The horde has taken [duchy_region.GetBaseName] and settled its warbands across the land. The Black Crusade for [crusade_title.GetName] still rages, but [duchy_region.GetBaseName] now answers to [current_crusade_beneficiary.GetTitledName].\n\nWith a new [current_crusade_beneficiary.GetLordLady] of [duchy_region.GetBaseName] holding the ground behind them, the warbands fight harder than ever for [crusade_title.GetName]. The rest of the [crusade_target_ruler.Religion.GetGroupName] realms will not stand for long.
Blood for the gods!
Let us see how long the dominion stands...
Cursed servants of Chaos!
I wonder what kind of life waits in [duchy_region.GetBaseName].
The Horde Takes [duchy_region.GetBaseName]

The horde has taken [duchy_region.GetBaseName] and settled its warbands across the land. The Black Crusade still rages, but [duchy_region.GetBaseName] now belongs to [From.GetTitledName] alone.\n\n[From.GetTitledName] still marches with the horde, yet the other warlords mutter that [From.GetSheHe] fights for plunder and land for [From.GetHerselfHimself] rather than for the glory of the gods.
A warlord who fights for himself fights badly.
Cursed servants of Chaos!
I took it. It is mine.

The dominion title of [old_crusade_title.GetName] was forged in war, and the rest of the world has never taken it seriously. Now that I hold a true title, I could set the old one aside and take up a crown that others must respect.
I will make the world respect it!
[old_crusade_title.GetName] becomes the true duchy of the region. The old Duchy of [duchy_title.GetName] passes into memory.
It has served its purpose. Let it go.
Respected or not, I keep it.

Marching through [current_location.GetName], I come upon the camp of [other_crusader.GetTitledName]. [other_crusader.GetSheHeCap] bids me share [other_crusader.GetHerHis] fire for a night, so that two lords sworn to the Black Crusade for [crusade_title.GetBaseName] might know each other better before the killing starts again.
I will gladly share your fire.
I came here to kill, not to make friends.

These last days in [current_location.GetName] have shown me how far I am from home. The [current_location.Culture.GetName] folk eat, pray and quarrel in ways I hardly understand, and some of them have been kinder to my men than I expected.
I should learn what I can of these people while I am here.
I will make a friend of one of them.
They are the enemy. I will not forget it.
I feel more [current_location.Culture.GetName] than [Root.Culture.GetName] these days.
The host crosses an old battlefield near [current_location.GetName]. The dead lie where they fell, picked over by crows, friend and foe in the same mud. Our people met hard resistance here.
Bury our own.
Bury them all. They fought bravely.
Take their skulls. Khorne will want them.
There will be coin on these bodies.

A merchant caravan bound for [current_location.GetName] rolls up beside my column. Its master flashes me a gap-toothed grin and pulls back a cloth to show me his finest wares: regalia fit for a lord of these lands, bought or stolen who knows where.
That piece. I will take it.
Kill them all and take everything.
Hand over your purses and live.
Not today. On your way.

When I set out on this war, I never thought I would miss home so much. My warriors look to me, so I keep my face hard and my voice steady, but at night I think of my own hall and my own bed, and the road ahead seems very long.
I have to keep going.
I will ease off and stop driving myself so hard.
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] will see me through.
As we make camp near [current_location.GetName], a comet with two burning tails crosses the night sky. The whole camp is on its feet, and every warrior has a different tale of what it means.
It is a sign! [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] is with us!
Enough gawping. Back to work.
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] speaks to me!
Let us give thanks to [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] for this wonder.

A band of my warriors has beheaded a row of villagers in [current_location.GetName], for no reason but that they keep the [current_location.Religion.GetName] faith. The heads are set on stakes along the road for the rest of the host to see.
Leave some for me!
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] would never want this.
A hard lesson, but these people must learn it.

In [current_location.GetName], deep in enemy country, we come upon a handful of [Root.GetCrusadeReligiousMinorityGroup] who have kept their faith in secret. They greet us as long-lost kin and give my warriors food and a dry place to sleep.
Let me help you spread the faith here, friends.
One of you should come back with me to [Root.Capital.GetName].
Thank you for your welcome.
Walking the streets of [current_location.GetName], I feel someone bump into me as a boy darts away down an alley. He is holding a purse that looks a great deal like mine!
No matter. There was little left in it.
Find that brat and make him pay.
A boy with hands that quick could be useful.

The locals of [current_location.GetName] whisper of a hedge sorcerer living alone in the hills. I go to see him with a few of my guards. He is old and half blind, but his hut is stacked with books and charms, and he offers to share what he knows.
I will learn what he has to teach.
Kill him. The books are worth more than he is.

Passing through [current_location.GetName], we come upon a festival to old gods that the locals still keep. There is drink, dancing and fire in the fields, and it puts me in mind of the harvest feasts at home.
Let us join the feast!
This is not fit for a true [Root.Religion.GetName] warrior.
What if these old gods are the true ones?

I wake after a long night of drinking with my men, sure that I heard the voice of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName]. It lasted only a moment, but it told me to give everything I have to this war and to the brothers who fight beside me.
It must be so!
Maybe I should not have had that last cup.
I am called to take the vows of [decided_holy_order.PrimaryTitle.GetName]!

As we make camp for the night, riders in the colours of a holy order come in from the dark. They are led by [holy_order_meeting.GetTitledName], who has them settle beside us. As I make ready for sleep, [holy_order_meeting.GetFirstName] asks if I will sit up with [holy_order_meeting.GetHerHim] by the fire and talk.
Gladly. This is a friendship worth making.
Forgive me, but it is late.

My warriors and I end the evening in a tavern in [current_location.GetName]. A pretty serving girl has hardly left my side all night, and as I make for my room she makes it plain that she would like to come with me.

My warriors and I end the evening in a tavern in [current_location.GetName]. A handsome serving boy has hardly left my side all night, and as I make for my room he makes it plain that he would like to come with me.
I did not come here to bed the enemy.
No one will know about one night.
Come back with me to my court!
My warriors have grown sullen these last days. The long halt in [current_location.GetName] has worn them down, and they grumble more than they sharpen their blades.
I will drill them back into a fighting host!
They need something to fight for!
I will make them unstoppable.
The Prophet of Doom

The horde was broken, but the wounds of the Black Crusade are still raw. In [shepherds_province.GetName] a wild-eyed prophet preaches in the market squares that the war is not over. The gods, he cries, are angry that the faithful let the servants of the Dark Gods crawl home alive.\n\nFlagellants follow him from town to town, whipping their backs bloody. Ruined farmers, grieving widows and penniless apprentices take up his cry. The lords are weary of war and want none of it, and the commons are starting to look at them with hard eyes.
This will not end well...
The Penitent Host

With a great cry, [shepherds_leader.GetFirstName] the Prophet leads the Penitent Host out of [shepherds_province.GetName]. Thousands of men and women of the [shepherds_province.Culture.GetName] lands march with [shepherds_leader.GetHerHim], flagellants and zealots at their head, and not a single lord or lady among them.

They swear they are guided by the hand of [shepherds_leader.Religion.GetHighGodName], and they march north to carry the war into [kingdom_target.GetBaseName], the land that sent the horde. It is a long road through hard country, with no supply train and few friends along the way.

Can faith alone carry a rabble so far?
Peasants, marching to war against Chaos?
Peasants? Let them come.
The Penitent Broken

At last [From.GetFirstName] the Prophet ordered [From.GetHerHis] host to lay down its arms, for the losses against [FromFrom.GetTitledName] had grown too great to bear. Most of the penitent were put to the sword where they stood, and [From.GetFirstName] was dragged to [FromFrom.Capital.GetName] in chains to show the world what becomes of peasants who make war on their betters.\n\nFew ever believed a rabble could beat the armies of [FromFrom.PrimaryTitle.GetName].
As expected.
The Penitent Kingdom of [From.PrimaryTitle.GetBaseName]

With flails, pitchforks and smith's hammers, the Penitent Host storms the last strongholds of [From.PrimaryTitle.GetBaseName]. The doubters were many, but nothing could turn the faithful from their road.\n\nThe world watches in wonder and alarm as [From.GetDynName] takes the throne. A peasant no longer, no one can deny [From.GetHerHis] right to it, for who but [From.Religion.GetHighGodName] could have led [From.GetTitledFirstName] to victory?
The peasants won?
The Penitent Scatter

Without [From.GetFirstName] the Prophet, the Penitent Host is falling apart. [From.GetHerHisCap] death broke the heart of the rabble, and the penitent have fled to every corner of the world, whipping themselves as they go.\n\nWho truly believed that peasants could win a war on their own?
As expected.

The ragged thousands of the Penitent Host are camped outside [current_location.GetName], singing hymns and whipping their backs. Their prophet, [shepherds_leader.GetFirstName], has come to my gate to ask for aid in their holy war.
They may pass through, but quickly.
A holy war against Chaos? Count me in.
You join the war of the Penitent Host.
I will send you some of my men.
You send some of your soldiers to march with §Y[shepherds_leader.GetFirstName]§! in [shepherds_leader.GetHerHis] holy war.

The zealots of the Penitent Host demand that I drive the Strigany out of my realm. Their prophet, [shepherds_leader.GetFirstName], says the wanderers are the servants and cattle of the vampire lords, and that the gods will not grant victory while they are suffered to live among the faithful.
I rule [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName], not you!
Perhaps [shepherds_leader.GetSheHe] is right.

As expected, the zealots of the Penitent Host have brought trouble to [current_location.GetName]. They have flogged a miller they called a sinner, burned a barn they called cursed, and emptied the granaries to feed themselves. My people look to me to be rid of them.
It is safer to let them pass through.
The §RProsperity§! of §Y[current_location.GetName]§! will fall.
Anyone who plunders my lands answers for it.
You will treat §Y[From.GetTitledName]§! and [From.GetHerHis] host as enemies in your lands.

As the Penitent Host moves through [current_location.GetName], a good number of its followers stay behind and settle in the area. It seems some of them have had second thoughts about the long road north.
We can always use more hands.
Deserters have no place in [current_location.GetName]. Back to the march!

[local_bishop.GetTitledName] preached that the Penitent Host was a rabble of thieves and madmen. The zealots of [From.GetFirstName] dragged [local_bishop.GetHerHim] from the temple, named [local_bishop.GetHerHim] a heretic and a friend of witches, and burned [local_bishop.GetHerHim] in the square.
[local_bishop.GetSheHeCap] brought this on [local_bishop.GetHerselfHimself].
It is time to put an end to them.
You will treat §Y[From.GetTitledName]§! and [From.GetHerHis] host as enemies in your lands.
I never liked [local_bishop.GetFirstName] anyway.

The cursed [From.Religion.GetName] fanatics of the Penitent Host have marched into [current_location.GetName] and are already causing trouble among the people. If this goes on, it is only a matter of time before the province is in uproar.
Better to wait for them to leave.
The §RProsperity§! of §Y[current_location.GetName]§! will fall.
I will drive them out myself!
You will treat §Y[From.GetTitledName]§! and [From.GetHerHis] host as enemies in your lands, and so will your liege.
Carve Out a Dominion
We hold the entire §YDuchy of [Root.GetBaseName]§!.\n\nIf we wish, we can settle a warband here, take the duchy and carve out a dominion for the gods in enemy land.

§BSons of Abraham:§! The Penitent Host
After a failed Black Crusade, the Old World faithful may rise as the Penitent Host and march north.
The Penitent Host never marches.

The banners of the Black Crusade fly over [crusade_title.GetBaseName] and my warband stands on its soil at last. The warlord's sorcerers daub the eight-pointed star on my brow in blood that will not wash off. Whatever I was before, I am now a crusader of the Dark Gods, marked for all to see.
The gods see me now.

From the ridge I see the lands of [crusade_title.GetBaseName] spread out below: fat fields, timid villages, the smoke of hearths that do not yet know what is coming. My warriors howl and beat their shields. We are the first of the Black Crusade to come this far, and the gods will remember it.
Let them hear us coming!

The gates of [From.GetName] are broken and its defenders hang from its walls. The capital of [crusade_title.GetBaseName] is mine! Its temples burn, its relics are dragged through the mud, and the warriors of the Black Crusade chant my name. The Dark Gods have seen who took the prize.
Blood for the gods, skulls for the throne!

A rider black with soot brings word: [From.GetBestName] has stormed [From.GetHerHis] way into the capital of [crusade_title.GetBaseName]. The heart of the target lands is ours, and the Black Crusade roars with victory.
The gods favour us!

The defenders have come back in force and thrown my warriors from the walls of [From.GetName]. The capital of [crusade_title.GetBaseName] is lost. The warlord's champions sneer at me, and I can feel the gaze of the Dark Gods turn away in disgust.
I will take it back, or die trying.
Grim news from the front: the capital of [crusade_title.GetBaseName] has been retaken from [From.GetBestName]. The Forces of Order cheer in their temples, and the Black Crusade has lost its prize.
Weaklings! The gods despise failure.

The Black Crusade gathers against [crusade_title.GetBaseName], yet my lord [Liege.GetTitledFirstName] sits in [Liege.GetHerHis] hall and has not pledged a single warrior. The omens in the entrails are clear: the gods are watching, and they are not pleased. Should I tell [Liege.GetHerHim] so?
I will write to [Liege.GetHerHim].
It is not my place.

[From.GetBestName] writes to me:\n\n'My lord, the Black Crusade gathers and every warband of the north rides to it. The Dark Gods ask where your banners are. I have read it in smoke and blood: those who hold back now will be forgotten, or worse, remembered. Pledge your sword, and let the gods see you.'
I will march.
When I am ready, and not before.

Three months have passed since I wrote to [Liege.GetTitledFirstName], and still [Liege.GetSheHe] has not pledged to the Black Crusade. Others ride south to glory while my lord lingers at home. [Liege.GetSheHeCap] will hear what I think of that.
Coward.

[From.GetBestName] writes to me again, and this time there is no respect in the letter:\n\n'The Black Crusade marches and you are not with it. I have stopped asking the gods to forgive you. They do not forgive, and neither will I.'
Let [From.GetHerHim] seethe.

Every warband worth its salt is riding to the Black Crusade against [crusade_title.GetBaseName], and my lord [Liege.GetTitledFirstName] has not pledged. My warriors grumble that we serve a [Liege.GetLordLady] who fears the fight. Should I tell [Liege.GetHerHim] what the camp is saying?
I will write to [Liege.GetHerHim].

[From.GetBestName] writes to me:\n\n'My lord, the warriors are restless. They hear of the Black Crusade and ask why our banners stay at home. They want blood, plunder and the gods' eye upon them. Pledge us to the crusade, or I cannot promise they will stay loyal for long.'

Three months have passed since I wrote to [Liege.GetTitledFirstName], and still we sit at home while the Black Crusade wins glory without us. My warriors no longer bother to lower their voices when they curse [Liege.GetHerHim].

[From.GetBestName] writes to me again, and the letter drips with scorn:\n\n'The Black Crusade has gone and we stayed home like old dogs by the fire. The warriors will remember who held them back. So will I.'
